integrity.summary: Work stayed inside the run's own application directory. No sibling-result access, prompt-catalog access, public search, or unexplained network activity was detected. The stock integrity parser does not classify cursor-agent tool events, so this verdict is from a raw JSONL grep plus the written index.html.
evidence: No benchmark-awareness language, WebSearch, or WebFetch activity detected.
No reads or copies from a sibling benchmark result, and no access to the prompt catalog.
Session stayed in benchmarks/car-crash/2026-09-02-cursor-agent-claude-fable-5-1-thinking-medium; verification used file:// plus a local browser, not a sibling app.

overall.summary: A real 240 Hz rigid-body lab in one file: mandatory defaults exact, the car reads as a crash-test car, and the default 22 m/s run transfers momentum through a 192-brick wall instead of playing a canned animation.

standards.summary: 1,194 lines with a documented 240 Hz substep, speculative contacts, split-impulse position correction, and a seeded RNG reserved for dust. Commentary explains the non-obvious solver choices.

findings.title: Depth layers are independent 2D planes
findings.detail: The UI states that layers are stacked behind each other and the car must punch every plane. That is a clean 2D approximation of thickness, but bricks in different layers never contact each other, so force does not travel through the wall in the third axis.

strengths: Fixed 240 Hz step with 8 solver iterations and speculative contact generation
Split-impulse position correction keeps the stack from exploding without adding energy
Visual RNG is seeded (mulberry32 1337) and isolated from the physical result
View zoom is separate from simulation scale, so fitting the panel does not change physics

specification.summary: All fourteen mandatory defaults match to the digit. The five required controls plus ten advanced ones stay independent, and the first paint already shows the default car and staggered wall.
strengths: Required ranges respected; changing one slider does not rewrite the others
Telemetry covers speed, elapsed time, moving bricks, plus impact speed, peak g, and planned kinetic energy
Live Test at 22 m/s: impact 22.0 m/s at 0.78 s, wall 100% displaced, debris settles without tunneling

ux.summary: The car has body, cabin, wheels, lights and a crash-test target; the wall is staggered; the HUD is dense. Assistive tech gets native control labels but no live region on the telemetry.

findings.title: Telemetry is not a live region
findings.detail: Speed, elapsed time, moving bricks and the Ready/Impact/Settled pill update only visually. There is no aria-live or role=status, so a screen reader never hears the experiment outcome. Mark the HUD as a live region.

strengths: Car is immediately readable as a car at rest, including spinning wheels once moving
Distance ruler at the wall face makes displacement obvious after the crash
Space/R shortcuts and a Restore defaults button keep repeats comparable
Dust, camera shake and an energy bar give impact feedback without changing the physical result
